about.title: Seaside Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Seaside's economy runs on a mix of hospitality, retail, construction, and logistics work, and each of these fields carries its own injury risks. If you were hurt while working, California generally routes your claim through workers' compensation regardless of who was at fault, but that's not always the end of the story. When someone outside your employer — a subcontractor on a job site, a property owner, or an equipment manufacturer — contributed to your injury, a separate third-party claim may be possible alongside your workers' comp benefits. Understanding which path applies, and whether both might, is exactly the kind of question our team can help answer. We don't charge for a consultation; we simply review your situation and explain the options, including deadlines that matter for reporting the injury and pursuing any outside claim.

whyChoose.title: Why Injured Workers in Seaside Choose Us

items.title: Understanding the Third-Party Angle
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party like a subcontractor or equipment maker may still owe you a separate claim. We can help identify whether that applies to your case.

items.title: Protection Against Retaliation
items.desc: California law makes it illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting a workplace injury. Our team can help you understand your rights if you're worried about your job status after speaking up.

items.title: Awareness of Reporting and Filing Deadlines
items.desc: You generally have 30 days to report a workplace injury to your employer, and any third-party claim carries its own two-year deadline. Missing either window can limit your options, so early guidance matters.

items.question: I was hurt at a job site near Fremont Boulevard in Seaside — does it matter who else was working there?
items.answer: It can. If a subcontractor, property owner, or another company working alongside your employer contributed to the accident, you may have a claim against them separate from workers' compensation. We can review who was involved and whether a third-party claim applies to your situation.

items.question: Can I still get workers' comp if the accident was partly my fault?
items.answer: Generally yes — California workers' comp is a no-fault system, meaning your own contribution to the accident usually doesn't bar you from benefits. This is different from a third-party claim, which typically involves questions of negligence. We can explain how each type of claim works for your case.

items.question: What if my employer questions or delays my injury report?
items.answer: You're required to report the injury within 30 days, and it's illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for doing so. If you're facing pushback or delays, our team can help you understand your rights and next steps.
